description: A script developer has written a utility script located at /home/user/scripts/backup.sh. However, the script is currently world-writable, which creates a security vulnerability because any user can modify or overwrite it. Your task is to secure /home/user/scripts/backup.sh by restricting its permissions so that only the owner (user) can read, write, and execute it, while all other users have no permissions to the file. After changing the permissions, verify your action by generating a log file at /home/user/scripts/permission_log.txt. This log file should contain a single line with the full output of the command that displays the file permissions and ownership of /home/user/scripts/backup.sh (for example, using ls -l /home/user/scripts/backup.sh), including permission bits, owner, group, file size, modification time, and file name. The automated test will check that: - Only the owner has read/write/execute permissions. - All other users have no permissions. - The content of /home/user/scripts/permission_log.txt is exactly one line, and contains the accurate permission information for /home/user/scripts/backup.sh after your change.
truth: Before task execution: - The file /home/user/scripts/backup.sh exists and is world-writable with permissions -rwxrwxrwx (mode 777). - The owner and group of /home/user/scripts/backup.sh is user. - /home/user/scripts/permission_log.txt must not exist before the task. After task execution: - The file /home/user/scripts/backup.sh has permissions set to -rwx------ (mode 700), owner user, group user, and retains its contents. - The file /home/user/scripts/permission_log.txt exists and contains exactly one line: it is the literal output of ls -l /home/user/scripts/backup.sh executed by user after the permissions change. - Example content of /home/user/scripts/permission_log.txt: -rwx------ 1 user user <FILESIZE> <MONTH> <DAY> <TIME> /home/user/scripts/backup.sh - There are no additional lines or content in the log file.
